## Enrichment Result Variables

@tbl-enrichment-variables summarises the variables stored in the
`enrichment_long` table generated by `scripts/06_03_enrichment_analyses.R`.
The table combines ORA and GSEA outputs from GO, ReactomePA, and MSigDB
Reactome analyses.

| Variable name | Formula | Biological function | Scale |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `study`, `technique` | Fixed provenance labels from the analysis script. | Identify the dataset and enrichment workflow that produced each result. | Categorical labels. |
| `celltype` | Cell-type stratum used to subset the differential-expression table. | Links each pathway term to the developmental state in which enrichment was tested. | Categorical label. |
| `method` | `ORA` or `GSEA`. | Distinguishes thresholded over-representation from ranked gene-set enrichment. | Categorical label. |
| `database` | Annotation source, for example `GO_BP`, `ReactomePA_Reactome`, or `MSigDB_M2_CP_REACTOME`. | Defines the biological vocabulary used for pathway or process interpretation. | Categorical label. |
| `ID`, `Description` | Term identifier and human-readable term name. | Name the enriched biological process, pathway, or gene-set concept. | Categorical labels. |
| `pvalue` | ORA: hypergeometric/Fisher tail probability; GSEA: permutation or fgsea enrichment probability. | Raw evidence against no enrichment for a term before multiple-testing correction. | $0 \leq p \leq 1$; smaller is stronger evidence. |
| `p.adjust`, `qvalue` | `p.adjust`: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR; `qvalue`: estimated false-discovery rate where available. | Multiple-testing controlled evidence; these should be interpreted together as FDR-type quantities. | $0 \leq \mathrm{FDR} \leq 1$; smaller is stronger evidence. |
| `neglog10_padj`, `sig_fdr` | $\mathrm{neglog10\_padj} = -\log_{10}(\max(p.adjust, \epsilon))$; `sig_fdr = p.adjust < 0.10`. | Plotting and filtering variables for FDR-supported biology. | `neglog10_padj`: $[0, \infty)$; larger is stronger. `sig_fdr`: `TRUE`/`FALSE`. |
| `GeneRatio`, `BgRatio`, `Count` | `GeneRatio` $= k/n$; `BgRatio` $= M/N$; `Count` $= k$. | ORA overlap summary: how many significant DE genes from the query fall in a term relative to the query and background universes. | Ratios in $[0, 1]$; `Count` is a non-negative integer. |
| `RichFactor`, `FoldEnrichment`, `zScore` | $\mathrm{RichFactor}=k/M$; $\mathrm{FoldEnrichment}=(k/n)/(M/N)$; `zScore` is a signed ORA summary from up- and down-regulated term genes. | Quantifies ORA effect size and direction; larger enrichment indicates stronger term over-representation among DE genes. | `RichFactor`: $[0, 1]$; `FoldEnrichment`: $[0, \infty)$; `zScore`: $(-\infty, \infty)$. |
| `geneID` | Delimited list of overlapping genes in an ORA term or core genes in a GSEA term. | Identifies the genes driving the pathway signal. | Character list of gene identifiers. |
| `setSize` | Number of genes in the tested gene set after mapping and size filters. | Measures pathway breadth; very small or very large terms are excluded by `min_gs_size` and `max_gs_size`. | Positive integer, here typically $10 \leq \mathrm{setSize} \leq 500$. |
| `enrichmentScore`, `NES` | `enrichmentScore` is the maximum running-sum deviation in GSEA; $\mathrm{NES}$ is the enrichment score normalised for gene-set size. | GSEA effect size and direction: positive values indicate enrichment near genes up in `neural_bias`, negative values near genes down in `neural_bias`. | `enrichmentScore`: usually $[-1, 1]$; `NES`: $(-\infty, \infty)$, often near $[-3, 3]$. |
| `rank`, `leading_edge`, `core_enrichment` | `rank` is the position of maximal GSEA deviation; `leading_edge` and `core_enrichment` describe the genes before that peak. | Summarise which ranked genes drive a GSEA term and where the signal appears in the ordered DE list. | `rank`: positive integer; others are character summaries or gene lists. |
| `log2err` | $\log_2$ Monte Carlo error estimate from the fgsea p-value calculation. | Quality-control measure for numerical stability of GSEA p-values. | $(-\infty, \infty)$; smaller uncertainty is preferable. |

: Interpretation guide for variables in the enrichment result table {#tbl-enrichment-variables}
